Method philosophy quotes

16 passages · 8+ thinkers in this selection

Why this theme matters

This theme page collects 16 English passages that touch method as a philosophical concern—whether as a concept to define, a value to pursue, or a problem to examine.

In the history of philosophy

Related discussions appear across Greek, Chinese, Indian, Islamic, Jewish, Japanese, Africana, and modern European traditions. Use the quotations below as entry points, then follow thinker pages for fuller context.

Frequently asked questions

What did philosophers say about method?

They approached method from ethics, metaphysics, politics, and lived practice. The passages below show several of those angles in compact form.

Where can I find philosophy quotes about method?

This archive page is organized for that search intent: verified English quotations, with links to thinkers and related themes.

How should I read these quotations?

Read the sentence first, then check school and source. A quotation is a doorway into an argument, not a substitute for the surrounding text.

  11. History is a discipline that has a large number of approaches. Its useful aspects are very many. Its goal is distinguished.

  12. By decolonization, I mean divesting African philosophical thinking of all undue influences emanating from our colonial past. The crucial word in this formulation is "undue".
    Kwasi Wiredu
    Africana Philosophy
  13. On the negative side, avoiding or reversing through a critical conceptual self-awareness the unexamined assimilation in our thought of the conceptual frameworks embedded in the foreign philosophical traditions that have had an impact on African life and thought. And, on the positive side, exploiting as much as is judicious the resources of our own indigenous conceptual schemes in our philosophical meditations.
    Kwasi Wiredu
    Africana Philosophy
  14. By 'African philosophy' I mean a set of texts, specifically, the set of texts written by Africans and described as philosophical by their authors themselves.
    Paulin Hountondji
    Africana Philosophy
  15. In fact, it is an ethnological work with philosophical pretensions, or more simply, if I may coin the word, a work of 'ethnophilosophy'.
    Paulin Hountondji
    Africana Philosophy
  16. To philosophize soberly and accurately is to distinguish carefully what belongs to the mind from what belongs to the living body.
    Anton Wilhelm Amo
    Africana Philosophy
